newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total head says productivity rises - paper.
newsitem.headline: Total head says productivity rises - paper.

text.p: Thierry Desmarest, chairman of oil group Total SA declined to give a 1996 profit forecast to newspaper L'Agefi but said the company's productivity was rising.

"We refuse to make comments about forecasts. Our first half results were good," Desmarest said in an interview. "Half of the explanation was due to internal factors and, for about the other half, it was due to a better (economic) environment."
He said that productivity improvements should make a contribution to the second half close to the first half.
"We have a little bit less production growth, because we have as comparison a very strong second half of 1995," Desmarest said adding the company was contiuning to improve productivity.
"Oil prices are at very favourable levels. I do not know what they will be tomorrow," Desmarest said, adding that refining margins remained "mediocre".
